claims.claim: Hong Kong should not impose a hard cap on starting rents in subdivided units.
Regulation should be tightened narrowly with security of tenure and a light, indexed band on starting rents.
A hard cap could hurt the households it is meant to help.
Tenants pay a 15 to 25 percent premium per square foot.
Real rent burden has risen from 31 to 34 percent of income.
Mr Chan pays about a third of his income for 120 sq ft.
Mrs Wong has no written agreement and says the ordinance changed nothing.
Long-run supply elasticity in marginal housing is estimated at 0.31–0.48.
A 10 percent cap-induced rent cut removes roughly 3–5 percent of stock over five years.
A 15 percent cut in initial rents transfers about HK$900 per month to incumbents but leaves 3,000–4,000 households per year unable to enter the segment.
The losers from a hard cap are the population the cap intends to protect.
Stock grew from 100,800 units in 2019 to 111,200 in 2025.
The 2021 ordinance is second-generation control, capping increases within tenancies rather than initial levels.
Second-generation controls show small or null stock effects, unlike first-generation hard caps, which show consistent contraction.
In Berlin, capped initial offers fell, listing supply contracted within a year, and after the law was struck down new-contract rents jumped above the pre-cap trend.
New York's second-generation scheme leaves initial rents and vacancy lightly regulated, and stock contraction is modest for that reason.
Where New York tightened in 2019, available stabilised listings fell as owners shifted units to other uses.
Inspection capacity covers under 6 percent of stock per year.
A band-based initial-rent cap would require a certifiable tenancy register costing an estimated 40–60 staff-years.
Enforcement would systematically miss the most exploited tail, including those with no written agreement.
A hard cap would invite compensation claims and judicial review, with litigation outlasting a Council term.
Landlords say owners will exit if returns fall below mortgage cost.
Mr Chan would accept any rent if the public-housing queue were three years instead of five and a half.
61 percent of surveyed tenants would trade a nominal increase for three-year tenure security and 74 percent for a faster public-housing offer.
Rent caps treat the price symptom of a quantity problem.
The defensible path is tenure security plus a published per-square-foot band defensible as rate-capping rather than confiscation.

cites.sentence: Tenants pay a 15 to 25 percent premium per square foot [D1p1], and real rent burden has gone from 31 to 34 percent of income [D2p2].
Tenants pay a 15 to 25 percent premium per square foot [D1p1], and real rent burden has gone from 31 to 34 percent of income [D2p2].
Mr Chan pays about a third of his income for 120 sq ft [D3p1].
Mrs Wong has no written agreement and says the ordinance changed nothing [D4p1].
The reviewed literature estimates long-run supply elasticity in marginal housing at 0.31–0.48, meaning a 10 percent cap-induced rent cut removes roughly 3–5 percent of stock over five years [D6p1].

The working paper models a 15 percent cut in initial rents as a net transfer of about HK$900 per month to incumbents, against 3,000–4,000 households per year—mostly new arrivals and newly formed households—unable to enter the segment [D6p4].
That arithmetic is uncomfortable precisely because the losers are the population the cap intends to protect [D6p3].
The 2021 ordinance is sometimes cited as proof that regulation does not reduce supply: stock grew from 100,800 units in 2019 to 111,200 in 2025 [D2p1].

But this is second-generation control—caps on increases within tenancies, not on initial levels [D6p2]—and the paper finds such controls show small or null stock effects, unlike first-generation hard caps, which show consistent contraction [D6p2].

But this is second-generation control—caps on increases within tenancies, not on initial levels [D6p2]—and the paper finds such controls show small or null stock effects, unlike first-generation hard caps, which show consistent contraction [D6p2].

Berlin illustrates the difference: capped initial offers fell, listing supply contracted within a year, and when the law was struck down, suppressed increases released and new-contract rents jumped above the pre-cap trend [D7p1][D7p2].

Berlin illustrates the difference: capped initial offers fell, listing supply contracted within a year, and when the law was struck down, suppressed increases released and new-contract rents jumped above the pre-cap trend [D7p1][D7p2].
The cap protected those already inside; the bill went to those still outside [D7p3].
Its second-generation scheme leaves initial rents and vacancy lightly regulated, and stock contraction is modest for exactly that reason [D8p2].
Where it tightened in 2019, available stabilised listings fell as owners shifted units to other uses [D8p3].
Inspection capacity covers under 6 percent of stock per year, and a band-based initial-rent cap would require a certifiable tenancy register costing an estimated 40–60 staff-years [D10p1].
If landlords reprice above-band, the first instrument tenants hold is complaint—but the least able to complain are those with no written agreement, like Mrs Wong [D4p1], and the newest arrivals.
Enforcement would therefore systematically miss the most exploited tail [D10p2].
A hard cap would also invite compensation claims and judicial review, with litigation outlasting a Council term [D9p1][D9p3].
A hard cap would also invite compensation claims and judicial review, with litigation outlasting a Council term [D9p1][D9p3].
The landlords say owners will exit if returns fall below mortgage cost [D5p2].
That is a real risk for a hard cap, though Mrs Wong thinks her landlords would stay because the units are their pension [D4p2].
Mr Chan does not name rent; he names the waiting list—if the queue were three years instead of five and a half, he would accept any rent to leave [D3p3].
The NGO survey finds 61 percent would trade a nominal increase for three-year tenure security and 74 percent for a faster public-housing offer [D11p1].
Rent caps treat the price symptom of a quantity problem [D11p2].
So the defensible path is tenure security plus a published per-square-foot band that regulators can defend as rate-capping rather than confiscation [D9p2].
